result.summary:
Modern now shows Arcade's own picture for every vehicle set that has no 3D model. Sprite sets use one MultiMesh per sheet: traffic and police have 17 ortho angles, player cars 21 perspective angles. The cell is picked exactly like RoadRenderer; a unit test checks it frame by frame against Arcade's own code. Near cars are folded onto rear and flank where Arcade warps, and the rows below the ground line lie on the road. Light is Arcade's _modulate (unit test, error below 1e-4). Buses and trucks become real textured boxes per part, articulated like R3's groups. Sets with a model are untouched; the switch is ModelDB.has_model, with no set ids in code.

Measured against Arcade at S1:
- Player picture for kombi, sportwagen and gran_turismo: rectangle 0.0 px, drawn pixels 2–3 px.
- Traffic at 20/60/150 m: 2/2/1 px; bus: 3 px.
- Brightness: −0.8 to +2.7 % by day; at night −6.0 % (kombi) and −1.8 to −3.6 % (light-coloured van).
- A stand-in behind the crest at T2 changes 0 px by day and at night; SpriteDB.loads does not change while driving.

Two bugs found and fixed late: flat pictures were drawn 2.6 % nearer than their car, and the renderer darkened the sheets at night by up to 25 %.

Final gates on fbfd1b5: run_tests.sh passed (603 unit tests, 73 CHECK OK), golden.sh '20 von 20 identisch', all 6 modern render-check files OK.

Still open: the 3D path shows very dark values darker than Arcade's canvas (R1), a double-shadow risk once the road receives shadows, and R3's absolute 40 µs perf gate flips between ~36 and ~49 µs on this shared VM (the first full run failed only there).

deviations: The snapshot reports lod 'box' for every stand-in, plus a new field standin (sprite/boxtex/painted). This keeps R3's check_vehicles kasten valid without editing it.

Sprite stand-ins only get glows for rear lamps, rear indicators and beacons, which is what Arcade draws over its picture. A glow behind the picture plane moves in front of it with a compensated radius.

Only the player's perspective picture is pulled toward the eye (factor about 0.70) so the road does not cut it. Traffic pictures keep the car's true depth; their rows below the ground line lie on the road along the eye ray, 2 cm above it.
Night brightness is gated on a light-coloured car (van_white). A dark red sports car measures -11.4 % because of the renderer's dark-end transfer (measured), not because of the light.

The box-set coupling comes from AS1's semitrailer (kingpin 1.65 m behind the trailer front, 1.19 m high; tractor turns 0.6 m behind it), since the sprite manifest has no pivots. A box's front face shows Arcade's rear picture.

A stand-in costs about 10–14 µs more per car than a painted box (measured, alternating bench). Part of this is offset by a behaviour-neutral early return in _add_flares for unlit cars, which also helps models.
Tunnel and fog light are verified by the unit test only (identical to RoadRenderer._modulate within 1e-4), not by a render picture.
contract_issues: Renderer dark end (R1): very dark values come out darker in Modern's 3D path than on Arcade's canvas. Measured on the pixel-aligned player picture: 11->7, 19->16, 28->26.5 of 255, equal from about 56; R1's own nacht check shows debug road 6/13/27 vs Arcade 16/21/32. albedo_for removes the polynomial part; the rest needs the 3D buffer format or precision checked.
Contract §4.4.2 point 4 (no sprite sheets in Modern) conflicts with the lead decision: stand-ins need sheets. Kiel–Hamburg loads 18 sheets in prepare(), about 69 MB (estimated).
The A-4 manifest fallback 'box' now means Arcade's picture; the painted box is used only without a sheet. Docs §10.1/§10.7 still describe the painted box and should be aligned by the doc owner.
Double-shadow risk (inferred): with shadow_casters >= 1 the hidden box caster adds a sun shadow beside the sheet's baked shadow once R1's road receives shadows. A decision is needed.

R3's check_vehicles leistung (not my file) measures wall time against an absolute 40 µs. On the shared VM the same code is bimodal: 35.6-39.7 µs or 48.9-49.5 µs, a factor of about 1.3. Suggest measuring relative to painted boxes in the same process, or measuring CPU time.

Arcade bug (frozen file, Rule 1, not fixed): BoxVehicle.emit drops a part's rear face through double rounding (pz0 < z_lo). Seen for a bus at camera+60.3/62 m; computed for 0.1 % (bus) and 0.3 % (truck) of rear positions.
notes_for_next: AS2a/AS2b: any new model in the manifest replaces its stand-in with no code change. check_vehicle_standin then picks another model-less set, or reports 'nichts zu vergleichen' when none is left.
RINT-A: line 155 of vehicles.gd (the contact-shadow material) is unchanged, and stand-ins use the same contact shadow.
R1/R4: missing headlight pools on the road are the largest remaining night difference to Arcade in the pictures (not this package). Settle the dark end and the double shadow before the night gate.
check_vehicle_standin has 6 parts (spieler, verkehr, kasten, nacht, verdeckt, laden) and takes 4.5–7.5 min under load. --only= and --save=<dir> help when looking into a failure.
The perf margin is thin on this shared VM. Steam Deck performance and memory are inferred only, never measured.

The A/B picture tools (ab_inject.sh, ba_inject.sh, probe/inject_ab.gd) are in the scratch folder /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/v080/m1/R3E, not in the repo.
result.look_verdict: The vehicles themselves look like Arcade. By day, traffic, police, bus, semitrailer and the three player cars match in position, size, angle and colour; in the magnified crops they are the same pixels apart from filtering. Near cars fold the same flank as Arcade's warp. At night the tail, brake, beacon and trailer marker layers sit as in Arcade. Better than Arcade: pictures have real depth, so a crest hides them, and buses and trucks are real boxes without Arcade's missing rear face. Compared with today's painted boxes, the before/after pictures show the biggest step up. Worse than Arcade: R3's tail-lamp glows at night are smaller than Arcade's soft halos. Very dark parts are a few levels darker (renderer dark end). The baked light does not follow Modern's sun, and in bends the views stay limited to Arcade's cell angles. What dominates the A/B differences belongs to other packages: missing headlight pools, trees, guard rails, sky and moon in Modern.

Kein Vorgänger gefunden. v0.8.0 (2b41e16) vorgespult, dann R1, R2, R3, AS1b und UI1 mit --no-ff zusammengeführt. Konflikt contact_shadow: R2 behält die Datei, R3s Fleck heißt jetzt vehicle_shadow. R2s drei Kernzeilen sind drin, STRICT steht auf true (0 Bandspitzen).

„Ein Bild“ umgesetzt: Gelände und Fernboden liegen auf Render-Ebene 2 mit Lichtkegeln und Abblendlicht. Lampen der Requisiten laufen über add_lamps. Lack und Glas haben eine Spiegelquelle (gemessen mittags und abends). Rotoren drehen (3 Bilder), Varianten je Stück, Bodendecker in Kurven, die hellen Rauten am Horizont sind weg. leave_modern ist die eine Freigabe-Stelle, beim Beenden gibt es 0 Lecks, Pause, Rückfall und Freigabe sind Render-Prüfungen.

Die Gates fanden weitere Fehler der Zusammenführung, alle behoben:
- ferne Bremslichter bei 75 % 3D-Auflösung zu schwach (flare.gdshader),
- 2 Shader-Varianten mitten in der Fahrt (Aufwärmen jetzt je Modell),
- vier Prüfungen auf den Stand nach der Zusammenführung angepasst, darunter kern_zeit, die den ganzen Renderer statt des Kerns maß.

Gates:
- Import sauber, Golden 20 von 20.
- Render 13 von 13 Dateien (39 OK), Sicht 6 OK, Weg 2 OK, Modelle OK.
- ERGEBNIS: nur gfx verschieden.
- Kiel–Hamburg in Modern ohne Warnung je Bild, Kaltstart 0 Varianten.

run_tests.sh, 2. und letzter erlaubter Lauf: 673 Unit-Tests ohne Fehler, aber 1 Prüfung rot (kern_zeit 0,618 > 0,6 ms). Den Umfang der Prüfung habe ich korrigiert, die Datei läuft einzeln grün (7 von 7). Ein voller Lauf auf dem Endstand fehlt.

result.look_verdict:
Bei Tag auf freier Strecke (S1, S3, T1) ist Modern klar besser als Arcade: echtes Gelände mit Tiefe, Autos als Modelle mit Klarlack und Kontaktschatten, Leitplanken mit Pfosten, Bäume mit Schatten, drehende Windräder.

Schlechter oder fehlend:
- Zwischen Gelände und Hintergrund-Silhouetten liegt ein heller Nebelstreifen (S1 2–7 Zeilen, an T4 wie eine Wasserfläche), die Silhouetten sitzen 2 px tiefer als in Arcade.
- In Städten, an Tankstelle, Brücke und Ziel ist Modern noch nicht besser, teils schlechter: Tankdach (S2), Brücke (S4) und Zielportal (S5) fehlen bis R5/R6, die Häuser sind Arcade-Sprites.
- Die Kurveninnenseiten an T2/T4 sind kahl, der Fels an T4 fehlt.
- Nachts sind Abblendlicht, Rücklichter und Fenster gut. Den Laternen fehlt aber Arcades kräftiger Schein, der Boden ist zu hell (N1 +21 … +42 %) und Schneefall fehlt.
- Bei „Niedrig“ (75 %) sind ferne Bremslichter nach der Korrektur sichtbar, aber nur ein rötlicher Schein.
